nodes.dlaczego.text.t: "At night something shines in the mill, and I never lit it. Cold and deathly blue. The dog howls, the wife prays, and I count my losses. If you've got the guts and a strong stomach, have a look after dark."

nodes.kamien_o.text.t: Ostap goes pale, as pale as a man covered in flour can go. "From the sky? And why tell me that, when I can't sleep as it is? Good thing it's gone from here. And devil knows what else is lying in the rivers upstream." He spits over his left shoulder, because that's what you do.

nodes.mlyn.options.[kamien].text.t: The smith says it's a stone from the sky.

nodes.mlyn.options.[odlamek].text.t: I came by night. Found this shard.

nodes.mlyn.options.[zboze].text.t: A sack of grain for you.

nodes.mlyn.text.t: Ostap dusts the flour off his hands, though there's none on them. "The mill's stopped because the river's stopped, and the river's stopped because something upstream gave it a fright. I grind whatever they bring. Usually nothing."

nodes.odlamek_o.text.t: Ostap listens to the tale of the shard and the blue glow and shudders as if someone had grabbed him by the scruff. "That's what was shining? Small thing for so much fright. Whether to believe you, I don't know, but the dog's stopped howling since it left the mill. Maybe it's true."

nodes.swiatlo_po.text.t: "Doesn't shine. The dog sleeps, the wife doesn't pray, and I still count my losses, only now they're my own. A man can live with that."

nodes.zboze.text.t: Ostap peers into the sack, sniffs, pulls a face and sifts a handful through his fingers. "Half rye, half sand. I didn't expect miracles from the man who sent it. Tell Wrzosek he still owes me two mugs of beer, and that I remember."
